scripts.//build:web: must run after build:crypto - tsup rolls up types from node-opcua-crypto/web, which only exist once dist/ is built.
scripts.build: npm run build:crypto && npm run build:web && npm run build:test
scripts.ncu: npx npm-check-updates --deep -u -x env-paths,chalk,@types/node,typescript && npx npm-check-updates --deep -u -t minor
scripts.//check:package: verifies the published shape of both publishable packages: exports map, files globs, and the per-condition types a CommonJS consumer resolves. attw is what catches a CJS consumer being handed ESM types (TS1479 / FalseESM); a runtime require() smoke test does not. Run after build - it packs the real dist.
scripts.//ignore-rules: scoped deliberately - do NOT widen. crypto ignores no-resolution because (a) node10 is TypeScript's pre-'exports' resolution, where subpath exports cannot resolve at all, and (b) the browser condition points at the OPTIONAL node-opcua-crypto-web peer, absent by design. web ignores cjs-resolves-to-esm because it is an ESM-only browser bundle with no .cjs counterpart. Everything else stays enforced - in particular false-esm/false-cjs, the CJS-gets-ESM-types bug this gate exists to catch.
scripts.check:package:crypto: cd packages/node-opcua-crypto && npx -y publint && npx -y @arethetypeswrong/cli --pack . --ignore-rules no-resolution
scripts.check:package:web: cd packages/node-opcua-crypto-web && npx -y publint && npx -y @arethetypeswrong/cli --pack . --ignore-rules cjs-resolves-to-esm
scripts.check:package: npm run check:package:crypto && npm run check:package:web
scripts.//check:browser: proves through a real bundler that the "browser" export condition redirects to node-opcua-crypto-web and that the Node build stays polyfill-free. Neither tsc nor the vitest suite can see this - it only manifests during bundling. Run after build.
